Make a setup: one complete decision

Source: R/setup.R
decision_setup.Rd

A setup holds one complete decision: the decider, the questions, the reference images, the image settings and, if you want, a calibrator. decide() takes a setup in place of decider and questions. write_setup() saves it as one JSON file that R code, a Shiny app and an agent can share, and read_setup() reads it.

Usage

decision_setup(
  decider,
  questions,
  references = NULL,
  max_size = 768,
  upscale = FALSE,
  crop = "none",
  calibrator = NULL
)

Arguments

decider

A decider from decider_typesafe(), decider_openai(), decider_foundry(), decider_openrouter() or decider_systemone().

questions

One question from question_noul(), question_choice() or question_score(), or a named list of questions, as in decide().

references

Reference images for the answers, or NULL (the default), as in decide(): a named list in which each name is an allowed answer of the question and each element holds the images of that answer (paths, URLs or magick images). This release takes references with one question only.

max_size, upscale, crop

The image settings, as in decide(): max_size is NULL or one number of 1 or more, and upscale is TRUE or FALSE. They apply to the references now and to the inputs of decide(). A crop function works in R, but write_setup() cannot save it.

calibrator

NULL (the default), or a probably calibrator, for example from probably::cal_estimate_isotonic(), fitted on the output of decide() for this question: its truth is a factor whose levels are the answers, and its estimates are the .pred_ columns of the answers. A setup with a calibrator has one question. decide() applies the calibrator (see the value of decide()). To add a calibrator to a setup that exists, see Details.

Value

A setup: an S7 object of class decision_setup with the properties decider, questions (a named list), references (the prepared JPEG bytes, or NULL), max_size, upscale, crop and calibrator. It holds no key.

Details

decision_setup() prepares each reference image once, with the image settings of the setup (and with three color channels for decider_systemone(image_format = "images")), and keeps its JPEG bytes. So decide(), the file of write_setup() and read_setup() use the same bytes, and a run with path has the same hash whether it starts from a setup or from its pieces.

A model that reads only text cannot take references, and bad image settings are refused: the setup stops with an error before it reads the images.

To add a calibrator to a setup that exists, set its property: setup@calibrator <- calibrator. This works for a setup from decision_setup() and for a setup from read_setup(), whose references are prepared images that decision_setup() cannot take again. The setup checks the calibrator, as decision_setup() does, and its references, its settings and its run hash do not change. Then write_setup() stores the calibrator with that hash.

Examples

refund <- question_noul("Does the message ask for a refund?")
setup <- decision_setup(decider_typesafe("jev-1.13.0"), list(refund = refund))
setup
#> <decisions::decision_setup>
#> * Model: jev-1.13.0
#> * URL: https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone
#> * Questions: refund (2 answers)
#> * Reference images: 0
#> * Image settings: max_size = 768, upscale = FALSE, crop = "none"
#> * Calibrated: no
